questions.stem: Which enzyme pair together bypasses the irreversible pyruvate kinase step of glycolysis?
questions.explanation: Pyruvate → OAA (pyruvate carboxylase, biotin, ATP) → PEP (PEPCK, GTP). A: G6Pase bypasses hexokinase. C: PDH and citrate synthase are oxidative, not gluconeogenic. D: FBPase bypasses PFK-1; aldolase is reversible. E: These aren't bypass enzymes.

questions.stem: During a prolonged fast, which compound can the liver use for net glucose synthesis?
questions.explanation: Hepatic glycerol kinase phosphorylates glycerol, which is oxidized to DHAP, a glycolytic intermediate. A: Acetyl-CoA's two carbons are lost as 2 CO₂ in the TCA cycle, so there is no net oxaloacetate. B, C: Leucine and lysine are the only exclusively ketogenic amino acids. E: Acetoacetate is a ketone body made from acetyl-CoA and gives no net glucose.

questions.stem: During fasting, which signal most directly activates hepatic pyruvate carboxylase?
questions.explanation: Fatty acid oxidation floods the liver with acetyl-CoA, an allosteric activator of pyruvate carboxylase. A: Insulin opposes gluconeogenesis. B: F2,6BP inhibits FBPase and activates glycolysis. D: AMP inhibits FBPase. E: Citrate isn't the activator of pyruvate carboxylase.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man is found confused after 2 days of binge drinking with little food. Blood glucose is 40 mg/dL and lactate is elevated. Which change in the liver best explains the hypoglycemia?

options.E: Activation of pyruvate carboxylase by ethanol

questions.explanation: Alcohol dehydrogenase raises the cytosolic NADH/NAD⁺ ratio, blocking lactate → pyruvate and malate → oxaloacetate, so gluconeogenesis fails once glycogen is depleted; mild lactic acidosis follows. B: The ratio rises. C: Induction would increase glucose output. D: Glycogen is depleted after days of little food. E: Ethanol doesn't activate pyruvate carboxylase.

questions.stem: A 6-month-old girl has lactic acidosis, hypotonia, seizures and developmental delay. Lactate, pyruvate and alanine are elevated; blood glucose is normal. Thiamine doesn't help. Which dietary approach is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: PDH deficiency, the most common cause of congenital lactic acidosis: pyruvate can't become acetyl-CoA, so a ketogenic diet supplies acetyl-CoA from fat, bypassing PDH. A: Carbohydrate increases pyruvate and lactate. B: Alanine adds more pyruvate. C: Cornstarch is for von Gierke disease. D: Biotin is the cofactor of pyruvate carboxylase, not PDH.

questions.stem: Glucagon promotes hepatic gluconeogenesis partly by phosphorylating which glycolytic enzyme, inactivating it?
questions.explanation: PKA phosphorylates and inactivates hepatic pyruvate kinase, so PEP isn't lost to pyruvate. A: Hexokinase is regulated by G6P. B: Glucokinase is regulated by its regulatory protein, not PKA phosphorylation. D: Aldolase is unregulated. E: Enolase is unregulated.

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy has hemolytic anemia, jaundice and splenomegaly. Hemoglobin structure is normal. His red cells have low ATP and have lost their flexibility. Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
questions.explanation: RBCs lack mitochondria and rely on anaerobic glycolysis; pyruvate kinase deficiency accounts for >95% of inherited glycolytic defects, and low ATP makes RBCs rigid, causing hemolysis. A: PDH is mitochondrial, so RBCs don't use it. B: Pyruvate carboxylase is mitochondrial, for gluconeogenesis and anaplerosis. C: Glucose 6-phosphatase is in liver and kidney. D: Glucokinase is in liver and β cells; RBCs use hexokinase.

questions.stem: A 2-month-old is found comatose after sleeping through the night and wakes with IV glucose. Pyruvate, lactate and alanine are high, aspartate is low, and ammonia is raised. Vitamin supplements don't help. Which enzyme is deficient?
questions.explanation: Without pyruvate carboxylase there is no oxaloacetate: gluconeogenesis fails (fasting hypoglycemia), pyruvate spills to lactate and alanine, and low oxaloacetate means low aspartate for the urea cycle (hyperammonemia). B: PDH deficiency gives lactic acidosis with normal fasting glucose. C: Von Gierke disease doesn't explain the low aspartate and raised ammonia. D: OTC deficiency raises ammonia but not pyruvate or lactate. E: MCAD deficiency gives hypoketotic hypoglycemia with medium-chain acylcarnitines.
